title: Comparative measurement of potential activity limitations in hemophilia and intensified physiotherapy
summary: In recent decades, the joint health of people with severe hemophilia A and hemophilia B (coagulation factor VIII or IX deficiency) has improved significantly through regular substitution of the missing coagulation factors. In the past, even minor stressors could cause joint bleeds. Repeated bleeding can lead to chronic joint damage in the long term, known as hemophilic arthropathy. This causes pain, restricted movement, and joint malalignment and can have a major impact on the everyday lives of those affected—for example, through limited mobility as well as social and occupational burden. Regular physical therapy and appropriate exercise are therefore an important part of treatment. They strengthen muscles and joints, reduce the risk of further bleeding, and improve quality of life. This pilot study is investigating whether intensive daily physical therapy over a compact period of time can improve joint condition in patients with severe or moderate hemophilia. Over a period of 2 years, 10 patients with severe or moderate hemophilia A or B will be included. The patients will receive physiotherapy sessions several times a day over a period of ten days. Mobility, joint condition and functionality, pain, and quality of life will be measured before and during treatment, as well as at a three months follow-up after physiotherapy. Patients will undergo physical examinations and joint ultrasounds. In addition, patients will complete questionnaires at all time points to assess limitations in daily activities, pain, and quality of life. The results will show whether the therapy is effective and which outcome methods can best capture the changes to serve as a foundation for a larger clinical study.

interventions.name:
Patients with severe or moderate hemophilia and a 10-day intensive physiotherapy:
examination of joint health before, 1 and 2 weeks post start of physiotherapy and 3 months after intervention by sonography, physical examination, physician and patient questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Severe or moderate hemophilia A or B (factor VIII/factor IX < 5%)
•	at least one target joint (knee, ankle, elbow) 
•	continuous factor substitution or Emicizumab therapy
Exclusion criteria:
•	Acute joint bleeding in last 4 weeks
•	planned surgical procedures in observation period
•	severe co-morbidities
